annotation_method: Agent-authored annotations prepared from independently opened official source pages before observing extraction-model outputs. The catalogue supplies entity names for joining, while source excerpts supply extraction labels. Each excerpt uses source-order fragments with [...] marking omissions and contains at most 25 quoted words per unique page. EUR normalizes explicit euro/€ units. A minimum IELTS value describes an accepted route; ielts_only_route is false only when an alternative appears in the excerpt. Omitted or null extraction slots are unobserved, and non-null predictions unsupported by the excerpt count as false positives. Citation checks audit entity identity and the specified funding claim using the reviewed official page and quoted evidence. Independent human/instructor review is pending.

limitations: This small source-checked set is an agent-authored draft. It has no independent human adjudication or inter-annotator agreement measurement.
Eight funding excerpts emphasize explicit tuition/living terms. They do not provide a representative test of every programme, condition, nationality or intake.
Language and deadline excerpts deliberately leave funding support unresolved. A valid official URL does not establish every claim made beside it.
The extraction input is a bounded excerpt. Missing fields must remain unobserved even if the complete source page or catalogue contains additional facts.
Programme-name claims evaluate identity mapping through the official name/acronym and page context rather than verbatim equality to descriptive catalogue record titles.
Funding classifications describe the cited award scheme and do not establish current scholarship availability, application opening or individual eligibility.
The excerpted source text is frozen at access date 2026-11-12. Live pages can change, and current output claims outside the annotated names/funding values require separate review.
